steps.name: Sami Wetlands Shaman
steps.text: Ragna, Ragna.

steps.name: Sami Wetlands Shaman
steps.text: How should we welcome you?

steps.name: Sami Wetlands Shaman
steps.text: From either the north or the south, you were always the least likely to return of those who left.

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: I know no one invited me.

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: But I saw a vision in my crystal ball.

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: ...A vision of my brother's death.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: What a beautiful sculpture! Does the little guy in the nutshell really point the way?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: And this Originium crystal! What an unusual color!

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: How do you keep the crystal stable while sculpting?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: No, wait, isn't it dangerous to have a piece of Originium as a home decoration?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Analysis on the Originium ice crystal I brought back last time isn't finished yet, but more importantly... it's so beautiful!

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Let's see... I think I have a few coins left from my last trip to Ursus!

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Or do you only accept bartering, like the local Sami?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: I can spare a can of seasoning to trade... But that would mean Simone and Typhon would have to eat bland Sami food with me.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: ...We're Sami to begin with.

steps.name: Ursus Caravan Member
steps.text: What do you actually want, girl? We'll be on our way if you have nothing to trade.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Oh, sorry, was I too loud? Haha...

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: I didn't think the Ursus caravans would come all the way up here, bringing so much stuff I've never seen!

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: What did you say you needed, Simone?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: ...Simone?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: You really didn't hear, did you?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Wh-What?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Someone recognized her and asked for her help.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Some bodies have been brought back to the tribe, but they don't have a Snowpriest, so they asked Simone to check them instead.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Oh, so people died...

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: No wonder the market's been so quiet. No one seemed interested in talking.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Everybody looks so depressed.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: They didn't put up much for sale, either.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Let's wait for Simone, then. She insisted on coming to the market, so she can decide.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Is that okay, my friends from Ursus?

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: O water that flows across the land of Sami. Allow me to speak to your children.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: (Low humming)

steps.name: Grieving Apprentice Shaman
steps.text: Wind.

steps.name: Grieving Apprentice Shaman
steps.text: From the lowest branch of the old tree, to the torch in front of Grandma Vali's door...

steps.name: Grieving Apprentice Shaman
steps.text: O great merciful fate.

steps.name: Grieving Apprentice Shaman
steps.text: It is assented. Go ahead, daughter of the Santalla Tree. Here are their belongings.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: I am grateful to earn the trust of a root of Frost Maple.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: There is red frost on the weapons. They were in battle.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: Are these warriors from the northern front?

steps.name: Grieving Apprentice Shaman
steps.text: Yes, they left the tribe for the northern lands seven or eight years ago.

steps.name: Grieving Apprentice Shaman
steps.text: Who could have guessed that the two tribesmen who'd left home the longest, who were the least willing to look back, would come home on the same day?

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: Are you referring to the dead?

steps.name: Grieving Apprentice Shaman
steps.text: ...A brother and sister who had parted ways.

steps.name: Grieving Apprentice Shaman
steps.text: Fate has also brought you here today. Perhaps you should hear the story.

steps.name: Grieving Apprentice Shaman
steps.text: You must remember the great snowfall that covered half of Myrkwood.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: Of course.

steps.name: Grieving Apprentice Shaman
steps.text: Our clan was affected too.

steps.name: Grieving Apprentice Shaman
steps.text: Like the other clans trapped in the blizzard, we prayed for Sami's wisdom and braved the wind and snow to seek messages atop trees, all to learn how we might protect ourselves.

steps.name: Grieving Apprentice Shaman
steps.text: But we did not have a Snowpriest.

steps.name: Grieving Apprentice Shaman
steps.text: We prayed and prayed, but received nothing but silence.

steps.name: Grieving Apprentice Shaman
steps.text: There was no guidance from fate, and our shamans could not determine whether to stay or not, or if we left, to where?

steps.name: Grieving Apprentice Shaman
steps.text: That was when those two siblings stepped forward to lead.

steps.name: Grieving Apprentice Shaman
steps.text: But their thoughts took them in opposite directions.

steps.name: Grieving Apprentice Shaman
steps.text: The older brother answered Eikthyrnir's call and brought his band to the northern front, to stop the snowfall for the rest of the tribe and spare them the need to leave.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: I see, accepting guidance from a Snowpriest outside the tribe in desperate circumstances.

steps.name: Grieving Apprentice Shaman
steps.text: Meanwhile, the younger sister felt that we could not afford to wait for the snowfall to end.

steps.name: Grieving Apprentice Shaman
steps.text: Using her Arts to foresee danger, she led the rest of the tribe southwards, eventually settling here.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: It couldn't have been an easy journey.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: ...For either of them.

steps.name: Grieving Apprentice Shaman
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Grieving Apprentice Shaman
steps.text: So we can understand why they hated each other enough to never look back.

steps.name: Grieving Apprentice Shaman
steps.text: Ha, my sister and I butted heads for months after I broke one of her horn ornaments. What is a mere seven or eight years to their differences?

steps.name: Grieving Apprentice Shaman
steps.text: ...*sigh*.

steps.name: Grieving Apprentice Shaman
steps.text: The blessed words carved into the side of his drum are all faded now. I would have redone them for him, if he'd come back even once over the last few years.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: This drum...

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: There's no blood on it at all.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: But the shaman who owned it was clearly badly wounded.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: I suspect... he didn't have his weapon when he was injured.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: There's half a bottle of vodka in his fur coat.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: Ha, the bitter brew that the Ursus squeeze from steel. Did they drink with the Ursus by the fireside?

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: Who brought back these warriors' bodies?

steps.name: Grieving Apprentice Shaman
steps.text: An Ursus caravan. Why?
'Checking status of Black Mark. Liebafowl is about to trade with those upon water.'

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: Are they still here?

steps.name: Grieving Apprentice Shaman
steps.text: They usually don't stay for long. The path ahead is treacherous when the sun has set.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: Thank you. I must find them... and ask some questions.

steps.name: Grieving Apprentice Shaman
steps.text: Wait... will you come back, Santalla?

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: Hm?

steps.name: Grieving Apprentice Shaman
steps.text: We're a withering clan... We could use all the help we can get.

steps.name: Grieving Apprentice Shaman
steps.text: This ceremony means much to us.

steps.name: Grieving Apprentice Shaman
steps.text: It's not just a sendoff for the dead, but also a chance for the living to bid farewell to their homeland. The more learned shamans there are, the better protected our people will be.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: ...Clan migration.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: Nearly a hundred years later, does the Samivilinn once again guide you on a great migration to the south?

steps.name: Grieving Apprentice Shaman
steps.text: Yes. This time, the Samivilinn gazes upon us.

steps.name: Grieving Apprentice Shaman
steps.text: We can recognize the signs.

steps.name: Grieving Apprentice Shaman
steps.text: Newborns crying all night, dead beasts by ponds...

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: (Signs of fear.)

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: (Has demonic corruption spread all the way from the icefield to the southern wetlands?)

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: (Or could the Black Mark that Ursus placed on Sami be...)

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: I have an inkling of the signs you speak of.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: I promise I'll be back for the ceremony.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: But... I have other matters to attend to for now.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: The spirits of the dead are watching. The living must bring them peace.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Is it really that bad when you don't have a Snowpriest?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Is that enough of a reason for things to be going badly for the tribe?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Yeah.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: (Takes notes) 'Snowpriests protect their tribe through soothsaying...'

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: 'Tribes without a Snowpriest may be unable to detect impending Catastrophes.'

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: So a Snowpriest has to study like a Catastrophe Messenger then...

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: You don't become a Snowpriest just by studying.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: I've seen Snowpriests-in-training in the tundras, on the brink of death as they go through their trials.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Other tribes wait for a revelation from Sami. Those who become Snowpriests receive miraculous instructions.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Anyway, you should talk to Simone about it. All I'm telling you is to stop asking around the market.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: This tribe is like a sick hornbeast. It's going to get irritated if you keep poking at it and telling it to get up.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Sorry...

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Also, this bracelet you picked isn't just ugly, it's bothersome too.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Hehe, that was just an excuse to get you to come to the market with me.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: You're almost fully Sami by now. You don't need me to accompany you in the south, where metal things are plentiful.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Still, I feel better with you around.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: I'm not sure why, but I'm getting a bad feeling.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: ...Do your bad feelings have a habit of coming true?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Not really.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: I hardly ever get them in the first place.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Tell me more.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Did it feel like a mangler's shadow, or a crack on a great tree?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: No, it's not like that...

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Wait, a mangler? There are manglers here? Will you take care of it if we run into one?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: *sigh* I'll teach you to protect yourself again before we go.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: What I'm asking is, what form does your bad feeling take?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Hm...

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: To me at least, you call it a 'bad feeling' precisely because it's vague and ambiguous.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: It's like, I felt something come close, but failed to notice it.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Or like there's something huge just beneath the layer of snow, but I walked right over it.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Which Professor Mary says I do a lot, come to think of it.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Ah... Ah-choo!

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Hey, it's snowing harder.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Oh, there you are, Simone!

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: Have you seen an Ursus caravan?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Yeah. They gave me an empty flagon while saying stuff like 'His Majesty' and 'The border patrol won't like it.' Here.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: I was waiting for you to get back, to see if you needed to trade with them for anything, but they were in a hurry.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: ...So you let them leave?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: They went that way. You should be able to catch up.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: You're angry, Simone.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: What happened?

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: Sorry... I was just thinking about how to return the favor for their gift.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: Magallan, Typhon, the two of you head towards Čappat with the rest of the tribe. And be careful along the way.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: If there's a problem, don't try to deal with it, just run. Your lives come first.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Same to you, Simone.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: Heh, you needn't worry about me.

steps.name: Santalla
steps.text: I'll catch up with you soon. I promised to attend the funeral of these warriors.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: What are you thinking, Maggy?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: That's weird.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: I was going to ask Simone what the Sami writing on this flagon means.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: But I got distracted for some reason.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Well, I'll just put it away for now.

steps.name: Mild-Mannered Shaman
steps.text: They came back, Ragna.

steps.name: Mild-Mannered Shaman
steps.text: Your predictions are always so accurate.

steps.name: Mild-Mannered Shaman
steps.text: Tila came back empty-handed. She's the best hunter in the tribe.

steps.name: Mild-Mannered Shaman
steps.text: And my youngest son found a bracelet that had been lost for years. As you said, 'Fortune lies in deep water.'

steps.name: Mild-Mannered Shaman
steps.text: And...

steps.name: Mild-Mannered Shaman
steps.text: Dark death has befallen our warriors.

steps.name: Mild-Mannered Shaman
steps.text: Therefore, I must ask you: Why did you do it?

steps.name: Mild-Mannered Shaman
steps.text: Why did you lead us in the opposite direction, when your scrying pointed towards the north?

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: ...Sorry, I only came back to see my family.

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: If there are no other funeral arrangements... I'll take my leave.

steps.name: Mild-Mannered Shaman
steps.text: Ragna!

steps.name: Stern Shaman
steps.text: Let her go.

steps.name: Stern Shaman
steps.text: She is no longer connected to the land of Sami. We need not reproach the poor soul.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: How was it, Gitano?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: They still don't like you?

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: I predicted as much.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Well... at least you ran into an old friend on the way. That's pretty lucky too!

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: I can still hardly believe it. I thought I was hallucinating again when I saw you!

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: —Er, sorry.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: I heard someone died. Could it be...

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: It's okay. I came back because I divined my brother's death.

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: We'd been out of touch for a long time. We had our... differences.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: But the shamans aren't preparing for a funeral. Don't they have the most important role?

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: ...Your friend is sharp, Magallan.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: It's hardly a secret.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: People aren't normally so sad just to say goodbye to the dead.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Only when they never get a chance to.

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: ...You're right.

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: Seven years have passed. I thought new branches would grow from the trees, and that the people would be able to live in peace on this land.

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: But all I see is my kinsmen suffering from increasingly frequent disasters, and even being forced to move again.

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: Meanwhile, the shamans argue over whether to hold a traditional funeral.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Hm... but what use is a goodbye if you don't say anything?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: In the end, everything flies away like a fowlbeast, never to be seen again.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: By that point, it doesn't matter if you were the one to raise your voice and startle them.

steps.name: Mild-Mannered Shaman
steps.text: I... never agreed to not hold a funeral. Please don't bring that up again.

steps.name: Mild-Mannered Shaman
steps.text: They were fortunate to return home. How could we leave them to the long, cold nights, trapped by their mortal bodies?

steps.name: Stern Shaman
steps.text: This place will soon stop being our home.

steps.name: Mild-Mannered Shaman
steps.text: Which is exactly why they need the boat-sinking ceremony, so that the river may carry them home!

steps.name: Stern Shaman
steps.text: Disaster lies before us.

steps.name: Mild-Mannered Shaman
steps.text: I know—

steps.name: Stern Shaman
steps.text: —And they are part of it.

steps.name: Stern Shaman
steps.text: The rockhorn runs for its life, day and night, until it finally dies of exhaustion. It is a sign. On the northern front, we will blow the horn and stand watch at night.

steps.name: Stern Shaman
steps.text: They are all warriors.

steps.name: Stern Shaman
steps.text: A warrior does not die in peace.

steps.name: Mild-Mannered Shaman
steps.text: Wasn't that just a rumor?

steps.name: Mild-Mannered Shaman
steps.text: Fighting on the northern icefields did not darken your fate. Instead, you received Sami's revelation and blessing.

steps.name: Mild-Mannered Shaman
steps.text: Yet now you want them to stand vigil over their own bodies, until they rot and decay...

steps.name: Mild-Mannered Shaman
steps.text: Among them lies your favorite student. Even now he is listening to your cold words.

steps.name: Stern Shaman
steps.text: Then let him listen. He is a strong warrior. He will understand.

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: —You're right.

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: Why don't we ask the dead themselves?

steps.name: Stern Shaman
steps.text: ...It would seem living among the outlanders has given you blind courage.

steps.name: Stern Shaman
steps.text: But you know that we have long lacked a Snowpriest.

steps.name: Stern Shaman
steps.text: No one in the clan has heard the call since Grandma Vali's passing.

steps.name: Stern Shaman
steps.text: Or do you propose that we break from tradition and imitate those tribes that set trials for their Snowpriests, rather than wait for the call?

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: I... can try to divine their will.

steps.name: Mild-Mannered Shaman
steps.text: Ragna...

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: Yes, I'm asking you to entrust it to fate.

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: I won't take any questions. Just think of me as someone who goes back on her word.

steps.name: Stern Shaman
steps.text: Then I won't stop you from trying.

steps.name: Mild-Mannered Shaman
steps.text: ...Very well, if the clan tree raises its branches and lets you sail through, I won't stop you.

steps.name: Mild-Mannered Shaman
steps.text: We await the answer of the dead.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Weren't you going to Čappat? I thought you southerners were always in such a hurry.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Like when your tourists come to visit. Their, er, vehicles just drop them off somewhere empty, they all stand around a while, and then the vehicle takes them away again.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: You're right, I am concerned about Professor Mary.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: But my best bet for now is to gather as much information about Sami as possible, to make things smoother for the rescue team.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Plus, I want to spend more time with Gitano.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: At Rhodes Island, they always say that nothing can rattle her except losing at cards.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: So I never thought I'd see her looking so gloomy...

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: What about you, Typhon? Isn't your client down south in Čappat getting impatient?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: No idea.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: I don't actually know who the client waiting for me there is, or what they want me to do.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Probably another one who wants me to help deal with a problem quietly.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: You can tag along next time. It's amazing what they'll do to keep things secret.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Like, leaving a message on a wooden board in a hole in a tree. When it was just about removing a dead hornbeast.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: The shadow was no longer near the beast, but that just makes them even more scared. So they look to me to take care of it.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Sounds like people trust you a lot.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: So do they really keep their distance from you just because they think your bow brings bad luck?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Isn't that just like... Oripathy?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Oripathy? Of course not, it's nothing like that.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Do you no longer respect Simone because she has Oripathy?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: But me... I'm not sure I've fully tamed this bow, to be honest.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Hm... but you're the one holding it. If it's not working right, wouldn't that be like when my drones malfunction? You can feel when something's wrong, right?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Of course I can keep an eye on it, when I'm awake.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: But what about when I'm dreaming, and my consciousness leaves my body?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Do you southerners have a saying like this? 'The more people speak of doom, the clearer it casts its shadow.'

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: You don't? Alright.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: When I lived in Arges's cave, no one knew of me or my weapon.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: But things are different now. The more I help chase the shadows out of Sami, the more people begin to talk about me.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: So who can say when misfortune will suddenly catch up with me?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: I'm sure your bow will be fine! We've journeyed all this way together with no problems, haven't we?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Although I guess the plural of anecdote isn't data...

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Oh, what if you let my colleagues in Engineering analyze it? Maybe they could come up with an explanation I can actually understand.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: And they might be able to help you.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: My friend Mayer, for example, knows a lot about dealing with dangerous objects.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: And we're super close, so I'm sure she wouldn't mind me filling her lab with potentially risky weapons, haha...

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: But research can take a long time, huh. I can't exactly take your weapon from you for years.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Thank you. You're a hard worker.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: But I told you not to touch my bow.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: This is for me to deal with, and only me. That's what Arges said.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: ...What are you doing, Magallan?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Let go.
Magallan lets go without even thinking about it. The splash brings her back to her senses, and she stares at the ripple on the surface of the water.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Wh-What did I just throw in there?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: The flagon the Ursus trader gave you.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: You were scooping up muddy water from the marsh with it.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: I taught you to filter mud and sand with clothes, but... I don't think you forgot. You didn't look right.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Oh! You're right! I somehow got distracted again!

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: I need to get it back... It was a gift.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: You don't dare reach out, do you?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Yeah.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Give me your hand.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: You know a way to deal with this situation?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: ...Phew.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: I feel calmer now.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: That was amazing! With just a vine around my finger!

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Oh, you have one around yours too.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Yeah.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: But you shouldn't try to get it back.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Remember what Simone said? Be careful.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Alright...

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Strange... That was a defense meant specifically for demons.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Could Simone's warning have meant...

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: ...The dead have answered.

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: Most want to be buried.

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: One... remained silent.

steps.name: Mild-Mannered Shaman
steps.text: Silence means there is no objection, at least?

steps.name: Mild-Mannered Shaman
steps.text: We must respect the wishes of the dead.

steps.name: Stern Shaman
steps.text: ...Very well, we'll hold a funeral as usual.

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: Be careful when you get on the boat, Magallan.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Thanks!

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: This is how the wetland tribes do it.

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: The boats are launched once night falls. The river carries them to their final resting place, where they will sink into the water along with the boats.

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: Only then can the dead be freed from the shackles of the flesh to walk free amongst the trees, and travel with the flowing water to find their bloodline.

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: However, this funeral is also our farewell to our homeland.

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: Which is why we will also bring our belongings and travel along with the dead.

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: ...These boats will carry the dead home, and the living away from it.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Can Typhon and I come with you? We're not part of your family or tribe or anything.

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: Of course you can.

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: In fact, I'd appreciate it if you did.

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: I've long known that I'm just a lone wanderer, far from Sami... Still, it's painful to have to ride in a boat by myself while saying goodbye to my last blood kin.

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: ...At least being able to hold a funeral will comfort the tribe.

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: Both the living and the dead.

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: What is it, Typhon? Need a hand?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: It's just that your hand is so cold, Gitano. Like you've been standing in the freezing wind for a long time, and the best you could do was rub your hands together.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: There's something I've been meaning to ask you.

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: What did the dead tell you?

steps.name: Typhon
steps.text: Or rather, what was the 'silence' in your divination?

steps.name: Sami Wetlands Inhabitant
steps.text: The horn has been blown. Don't look back.

steps.name: Sami Wetlands Inhabitant
steps.text: Fate has instructed us to move forward. What was left behind will eventually return to us.

steps.name: Sami Wetlands Inhabitant
steps.text: Row.
There is no more talk. The shaman's song can be heard from the head of the fleet.
The dead follow their ancestors, as their names are read one by one.
A breeze rings a string of bells on the boat carrying the bodies.
The ceremony has begun. The fleet will not turn back.

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: ...I'm sorry.
The fourth time, I still saw the ceremony.
The fifth time, I asked... Lazal.

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: Lazal, there's something I want to tell you.

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: ...Or maybe it's something I wanted to hear you tell me.

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: The road away from that blizzard was long. The river never thawed.

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: I lived away from Sami, sailing with a boat of iron. It was so firm and steady that I couldn't help but dream back to how our clansmen dragged their boats across the river.

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: Many lost the strength to pull their boats. Some lost the strength to pull even themselves forward.

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: ...Too much was lost on that path. I dared not turn back.

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: But in the end, that's all there is to it. I dared not turn back.

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: We made opposing decisions, and even took up arms against one another, but the reason I never came back wasn't because I resented you.

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: ...But perhaps none of that's important to a warrior stationed in the north.

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: The leaves in the urn are almost burnt up.

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: So please, tell me...

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: Why do you—

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: Why do you still refuse to answer, brother?

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: Darkness, fog, darkness.

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: An empty crystal ball.

steps.name: Gitano
steps.text: Why do I see nothing?
